title: Determination of time lag by accurate monitoring of pressure decay in a new generation constant volume system
author: Leszczynski, Cao, et al.

steps.title: Install membrane and evacuate system
steps.instruction: Install the membrane in the cell, then evacuate the system to degas the membrane using vacuum pumps P‑400 and P‑401 while configuring valves to isolate sections as described, and evaluate leak rates after a full evacuation lasting more than 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Open FV‑13 and keep FV‑8 and FV‑9 closed to evacuate only the downstream section.
Open FV‑9 (with FV‑13 open) to include the downstream part of the membrane cell in the evacuation.
Open the bypass line (FV‑8, FV‑5, and FCV‑7 open) while keeping FV‑2 and FCV‑4 closed to evacuate the entire membrane cell.
Open FV‑2 (FV‑3 closed) via the bypass line to evacuate the upstream part (working and reference volumes).
Open FV‑6 (while FV‑13, FV‑5, and FCV‑7 are closed) to evacuate the working and reference volumes directly.
After evacuation, monitor pressure rise with absolute pressure transducers to assess leak rates.

steps.title: Record typical leak rates
steps.instruction: Document the typical leak rates for each system section as listed in Table 1.

substeps.instruction: Reference volume (FCV‑1, FV‑6): 6 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ Torr/s
Total working volume (FCV‑1, FCV‑4, FV‑5, membrane): 93 (100*) 9.0 × 10⁻⁷ Torr/s
Downstream volume (tubing) (membrane, FV‑8, FV‑10, FV‑11, FV‑12, FV‑13): 18 1 × 10⁻⁷ Torr/s (note: without a metal disk in the upstream part of the membrane cell).

steps.title: Re‑evacuate, set valves, and charge gas
steps.instruction: After completing leak tests, perform another evacuation, close valves in the specified order, configure the downstream receiver to include only tubing, introduce gas from TK‑400 into V‑101 and V‑100 at a pressure above the desired level, adjust valves to isolate volumes, and allow thermal equilibration.

substeps.instruction: Close valves sequentially: FCV‑7, then FV‑5, FV‑8, and FV‑13.
Configure downstream receiver: close FV‑10, FV‑11, and FV‑12; open FV‑9.
Introduce gas from source TK‑400 into V‑101 and V‑100 until the pressure exceeds the target for the time‑lag experiment.
Close FV‑6.
Open FV‑2 to allow gas flow through FV‑5 and FCV‑7.
Close FCV‑1 to isolate the working and reference volumes.
Allow the gas to equilibrate thermally with the air in the temperature‑controlled chamber.

steps.title: Adjust V‑100 pressure and start measurement
steps.instruction: Reduce the pressure in V‑100 to compensate for the expected expansion in V‑101, then initiate the time‑lag experiment by opening FCV‑7 while recording pressure changes in real time.

substeps.instruction: Using pump P‑400, partially open valve FV‑6 to evacuate V‑100 until the pressure drop equals the anticipated drop in V‑101 (proportional to the feed pressure).
The feed‑pressure‑to‑expansion relationship was previously determined with an impermeable film and recorded by APT‑1 and APT‑4.
Close FV‑6 once the desired V‑100 pressure is reached.
Disengage pump P‑400 to minimize system vibrations.
Open FCV‑7 to start the time‑lag experiment.
Simultaneously monitor and record pressure rise and decay with the appropriate transducers (e.g., DPT‑1, APT‑1, APT‑4), noting that DPT‑1 has an upper limit of 1 Torr.
